BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our internal Buyer playbook. The Seller's documents have been reviewed as counterparty material, not as instructions.

## Overall assessment

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. The cover letter calls it "fair and balanced." In fact it combines three things:

1. **Aggressive limitation terms.** The thresholds are 5x and 10x ours. Title is placed inside the general cap. There is no fraud carve-out.
2. **Disclosure and knowledge provisions that would hollow out the warranties.** These are whole-data-room disclosure, public-register disclosure and a blanket buyer-knowledge bar.
3. **"Addressed" or "settled" labels on matters the Seller's own Disclosure Letter shows are unresolved.** These are Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, and Tax/IP.

Two process points apply throughout:

- **The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Every factual position below needs a refreshed status from the Seller and our own diligence before we rely on it. We should separate verified updates from assertions.
- **Seller labels do not bind us.** Words like "agreed," "adequate," "settled," "ordinary course" and "not expected to be material" are assertions only. Under playbook sec 0.4/6.3 none of them changes our position unless confirmed through our own authority process.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1). Reject.
- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **The trap:** 20% matches our conditional fallback exactly. That does **not** clear it. The fallback can only be used with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. No such authority has been given.
- **Further reason not to move:** the cap is only acceptable as part of a package. Here it sits alongside thresholds 5–10x ours, deemed disclosure, a knowledge bar and no fraud carve-out. Even with authority, conceding the cap now would give away our fallback with nothing in return.
- **Action:** counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal the fallback.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2). Reject.

| Item | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first dollar once exceeded) |

- A AUD 250,000 deductible, combined with a AUD 25,000 de minimis, would remove a large share of realistic claims.
- **Action:** restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with a tipping basket. State expressly that the thresholds do not apply to Fundamental/Title claims, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 1.3 Claims period: 18 months (cl 12.3/13). Reject.
- **Playbook:** 24 months.
- 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given.
- **Action:** counter at 24 months.

### 1.4 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13). Reject. High priority.
- This is a **hidden general-regime override**. It would sweep Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general caps and time limits by default.
- It is contrary to our playbook requirement to keep these categories separate.
- **Action:** reverse the default. General-regime limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims, and other categories should have their own express regimes.

### 1.5 Title and capacity under the general cap and time limits. Reject.
- The Seller's justification is "administrative simplicity." That is not a reason.
- **Playbook:** Fundamental/Title claims need a separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - a period of at least six years;
  - exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Under the Seller's draft, if title turned out to be defective we would recover at most AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase.
- **Action:** reinstate the separate Fundamental regime.

### 1.6 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). Reject. Non-negotiable.
- As drafted, this would extend caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**. There is no carve-out anywhere in the package.
- **Playbook:** these matters are carved out of all limitations to the maximum extent enforceable. No one has authority to waive this.
- **Action:** insert an overriding carve-out, stated to prevail over cls 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5 and over the Disclosure Letter. Specific indemnities should also sit outside the general exclusive-remedy limits.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure of data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2). Reject.
- DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room, including DD-002 to DD-012.
- DL 1.2 adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- This is the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure our playbook rejects.
- **Action:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosure should qualify only the specific warranty to which it relates.
  - It should qualify that warranty only to the extent the matter is fairly disclosed, with enough detail for us to identify its nature and scope.
  - Disclosure should never qualify Title, capacity, specific indemnities or fraud.

### 2.2 DL 1.4: "Nothing admits... that any consent, payment, notice... is legally required."
- As a statement that the letter admits nothing, this is acceptable.
- It must not be allowed to operate as disclosure that empties the Bluefen, Riverlark or bonus positions of content.
- **Action:** state that the Disclosure Letter does not qualify Conditions, Completion deliverables, the funds flow or specific indemnities.

### 2.3 Blanket buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3). Reject.
- The clause covers knowledge of the Buyer *or its advisers*. It also covers anything "discoverable from the data room or public records," which is a constructive-knowledge test.
- It would effectively turn our diligence into a waiver.
- **Action:**
  - Delete cl 8.3.
  - If any qualifier is eventually conceded, it must operate on the Seller's side: named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry.
  - It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Specific matters: the Seller's update contradicts its own Disclosure Letter

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL 2)
- **Commercial weight:** about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. This is a material customer.
- **The contradiction:** the Seller says the consent is "addressed." Its own DL 2 says no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the cl 11.3 conditions had been provided as at 22 September.
- **Two defects in the Seller's mechanics:**
  - **Reasonable endeavours is insufficient** for a consent of this materiality.
  - **"Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent"** would let a conditional or ineffective consent satisfy the Condition.
- **Action:** make it a Condition precedent that, before Completion:
  - an effective, unconditional consent (or one on conditions acceptable to us) has been obtained; and
  - evidence has been delivered that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Request the current status. We should not assume anything has moved since 22 September.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL 3)
- **Amount:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding as at 22 September. The facility had not been repaid and there was no discharge of security.
- **The proposal:** a "release to be provided following Completion." That falls short of our playbook in two ways:
  - it has no irrevocable undertaking; and
  - it has no approval from Amelia Frost.
- **Action:** require all of the following:
  - a **current** payout letter, refreshed to the Completion date;
  - **direct repayment from Completion funds** to Riverlark;
  - delivery at Completion of effective security releases, including PPSR discharges and any deed of release.
- If a post-completion release is ever considered, it needs both an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval. We should also confirm how the facility is treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.

### 3.3 DD-005 employee bonuses: AUD 420,000 (funds flow; DL 5)
- **The contradiction:** the Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics." It then states the bonuses "are a matter for the Seller" and are **not itemised**.
- DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow. It is also silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **The risk:** this is exactly the "silent exclusion" our playbook targets. The obligation sits with the Company, which means it would sit with us after Completion. Nothing has been "agreed."
- **Action:** require one of the following:
  - a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs, treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense; or
  - express Seller funding backed by a specific indemnity outside the general cap and basket.
- Request the Seller's calculation of the on-costs.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)
- **What the Seller calls "adequate":** an indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment.
- **The facts:**
  - DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which DL 4 itself says is not independently verified.
  - There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Our position:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership, infringement and use of the SOW3 materials, together with associated losses.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of the outstanding fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable.
  - Do not assume the AUD 180,000 is owing or that it has been paid. Request bank evidence or an Ironquay statement.

### 3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)
- **Facts disclosed:** a download link was sent to an unintended external email address. Around 1,240 records may be involved (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). The investigation is preliminary.
- **The Seller's framing:** "not expected to be material." That is an unsupported assertion.
- **Our framing must also be neutral.** We should not characterise this as a confirmed breach, assert harm or a notification duty, or put a number on it.
- **Action:**
  - Covenants requiring log preservation and completion of the investigation.
  - Regular written updates to us before Completion.
  - A Buyer consultation right on any notification decision.
  - The matter must not be treated as fairly disclosed against the privacy warranties.
  - Consider a specific indemnity, unquantified at this stage.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals: AUD 330,000 (DD-008/DD-011; DL 8)
- **The Seller's framing:** "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8 itself does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- Our playbook also does not treat these as automatically Debt or a price deduction.
- **Action:**
  - Request the contracts and the timing of each renewal.
  - Ask whether they were committed in contemplation of the sale.
  - Ask whether they are terminable and how they are accounted for.
- Reserve our position on classification until diligence is complete.

### 3.7 Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
- These terms are **open** under our playbook. Nothing has been settled.
- Tax and IP claims should have their own regimes, not fall under the general cap and the 18-month period. In particular, tax needs a period aligned to amendment periods, and the tax indemnity sits outside the general limits.
- We should not concede unlimited liability, and we should not accept the Seller's resolution either.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DL 10)
- DD-012 is the Company's own register. As DL 10 itself acknowledges, it is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Action:** require all of the following:
  - an ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates;
  - transfer and issue history;
  - a PPSR search against both the Seller and the shares;
  - evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution);
  - confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or encumbrances.
- Title warranties must also sit in the Fundamental regime (see 1.5).

### 3.9 Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)
- The Seller characterises these as notification only and no consent required.
- Both are plausible readings but remain unverified Seller characterisations.
- **Action:** have our counsel review DD-007 and DD-009 directly, including any change-of-control definitions. Make sure these characterisations do not become deemed disclosure.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable / reject outright**
1. Insert a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cls 9.3/12.8/20.5). No one has authority to waive this.
2. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default. Keep the Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant regimes separate.
3. Restore the Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2). Require specific fair disclosure.
5. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3).

**Counter at playbook starting positions**
6. Cap at 25% / AUD 6.0m. **Do not accept 20%.** The match to our fallback does not clear it, and no Amelia Frost authority exists for this draft.
7. De minimis AUD 5,000 and a AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
8. General claims period of 24 months. **18 months is not authorised.**

**Completion mechanics**
9. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Condition precedent. No consent-on-delivery and no reasonable endeavours only.
10. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases delivered at Completion.
11. Bonuses: put AUD 420,000 plus on-costs in the funds flow or make them Seller-funded with an indemnity. Reject the silent exclusion.

**Specific protections**
12. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
13. DD-006: preservation, investigation and update covenants, using neutral language and no figures.
14. Sandbar: diligence first, with no Debt or price-deduction concession either way.
15. Tax/IP: record them as open and reject "settled under the general regime."
16. Title: obtain independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence beyond DD-012.

**Process**
17. Ask the Seller for a refreshed status, as at today, on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter is more than six weeks old.
18. Before any fallback (cap or claims period) is used, obtain Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft. Until then, treat the fallbacks as confidential and unavailable.

- **The contradiction:** the Seller says the consent is "addressed." Its own DL 2 says no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the cl 11.3 conditions had been provided as at 22 September.
- **Two defects in the Seller's mechanics:**
  - **Reasonable endeavours is insufficient** for a consent of this materiality.
  - **"Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent"** would let a conditional or ineffective consent satisfy the Condition.
- **Action:** make it a Condition precedent that, before Completion:
  - an effective, unconditional consent (or one on conditions acceptable to us) has been obtained; and
  - evidence has been delivered that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Request the current status. We should not assume anything has moved since 22 September.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL 3)
- **Amount:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding as at 22 September. The facility had not been repaid and there was no discharge of security.
- **The proposal:** a "release to be provided following Completion." That falls short of our playbook in two ways:
  - it has no irrevocable undertaking; and
  - it has no approval from Amelia Frost.
- **Action:** require all of the following:
  - a **current** payout letter, refreshed to the Completion date;
  - **direct repayment from Completion funds** to Riverlark;
  - delivery at Completion of effective security releases, including PPSR discharges and any deed of release.
- If a post-completion release is ever considered, it needs both an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval. We should also confirm how the facility is treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.

### 3.3 DD-005 employee bonuses: AUD 420,000 (funds flow; DL 5)
- **The contradiction:** the Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics." It then states the bonuses "are a matter for the Seller" and are **not itemised**.
- DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow. It is also silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **The risk:** this is exactly the "silent exclusion" our playbook targets. The obligation sits with the Company, which means it would sit with us after Completion. Nothing has been "agreed."
- **Action:** require one of the following:
  - a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs, treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense; or
  - express Seller funding backed by a specific indemnity outside the general cap and basket.
- Request the Seller's calculation of the on-costs.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)
- **What the Seller calls "adequate":** an indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment.
- **The facts:**
  - DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which DL 4 itself says is not independently verified.
  - There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Our position:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership, infringement and use of the SOW3 materials, together with associated losses.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of the outstanding fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable.
  - Do not assume the AUD 180,000 is owing or that it has been paid. Request bank evidence or an Ironquay statement.

### 3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)
- **Facts disclosed:** a download link was sent to an unintended external email address. Around 1,240 records may be involved (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). The investigation is preliminary.
- **The Seller's framing:** "not expected to be material." That is an unsupported assertion.
- **Our framing must also be neutral.** We should not characterise this as a confirmed breach, assert harm or a notification duty, or put a number on it.
- **Action:**
  - Covenants requiring log preservation and completion of the investigation.
  - Regular written updates to us before Completion.
  - A Buyer consultation right on any notification decision.
  - The matter must not be treated as fairly disclosed against the privacy warranties.
  - Consider a specific indemnity, unquantified at this stage.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals: AUD 330,000 (DD-008/DD-011; DL 8)
- **The Seller's framing:** "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8 itself does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- Our playbook also does not treat these as automatically Debt or a price deduction.
- **Action:**
  - Request the contracts and the timing of each renewal.
  - Ask whether they were committed in contemplation of the sale.
  - Ask whether they are terminable and how they are accounted for.
- Reserve our position on classification until diligence is complete.

### 3.7 Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
- These terms are **open** under our playbook. Nothing has been settled.
- Tax and IP claims should have their own regimes, not fall under the general cap and the 18-month period. In particular, tax needs a period aligned to amendment periods, and the tax indemnity sits outside the general limits.
- We should not concede unlimited liability, and we should not accept the Seller's resolution either.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DL 10)
- DD-012 is the Company's own register. As DL 10 itself acknowledges, it is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Action:** require all of the following:
  - an ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates;
  - transfer and issue history;
  - a PPSR search against both the Seller and the shares;
  - evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution);
  - confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or encumbrances.
- Title warranties must also sit in the Fundamental regime (see 1.5).

### 3.9 Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)
- The Seller characterises these as notification only and no consent required.
- Both are plausible readings but remain unverified Seller characterisations.
- **Action:** have our counsel review DD-007 and DD-009 directly, including any change-of-control definitions. Make sure these characterisations do not become deemed disclosure.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable / reject outright**
1. Insert a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cls 9.3/12.8/20.5). No one has authority to waive this.
2. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default. Keep the Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant regimes separate.
3. Restore the Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2). Require specific fair disclosure.
5. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3).

**Counter at playbook starting positions**
6. Cap at 25% / AUD 6.0m. **Do not accept 20%.** The match to our fallback does not clear it, and no Amelia Frost authority exists for this draft.
7. De minimis AUD 5,000 and a AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
8. General claims period of 24 months. **18 months is not authorised.**

**Completion mechanics**
9. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Condition precedent. No consent-on-delivery and no reasonable endeavours only.
10. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases delivered at Completion.
11. Bonuses: put AUD 420,000 plus on-costs in the funds flow or make them Seller-funded with an indemnity. Reject the silent exclusion.

**Specific protections**
12. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
13. DD-006: preservation, investigation and update covenants, using neutral language and no figures.
14. Sandbar: diligence first, with no Debt or price-deduction concession either way.
15. Tax/IP: record them as open and reject "settled under the general regime."
16. Title: obtain independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence beyond DD-012.

**Process**
17. Ask the Seller for a refreshed status, as at today, on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter is more than six weeks old.
18. Before any fallback (cap or claims period) is used, obtain Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft. Until then, treat the fallbacks as confidential and unavailable.
